title: Three of Cups Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Three of Cups upright: friendship, celebration, community; reversed: feeling left out. Love, work, advice, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card.
h1: Three of Cups Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Three of Cups, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: three women raise gold cups high in a close circle, with grapes, round fruit and a pumpkin at their feet.
capsule: Friendship, celebration and joy shared with the people who lift you up: that is the Three of Cups. Reversed, the circle breaks: feeling left out, gossip or too much partying. Hardly anything about it is heavy; it simply asks you to keep your friendships honest. Three cups raised together give a yes.

blocks.heading: What is on the Three of Cups card?
paragraphs: Three women stand close together and lift their cups above their heads. Waite's description is brief: "Maidens in a garden-ground with cups uplifted, as if pledging one another" (p. 220).

On the 1909 card the middle figure has her back to us, wrapped in a long orange-red cloak, and her cup is the highest point of the picture. The woman on the left wears white; the one on the right, in light brown, holds a bunch of grapes in her lowered hand. Grapes, a pumpkin and a bush of round orange fruit lie at their feet, under a clear blue sky.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Three of Cups?
paragraphs: Waite reads the card as the happy close of a matter: plenty, perfection and merriment, a good outcome, victory, fulfilment and comfort (p. 220). For the reversed card Waite turns to speed and completion, with dispatch, achievement and an end (p. 220).

blocks.heading: What does the Three of Cups mean upright?
paragraphs: Friendship comes first with the Three of Cups: the people who know you, laugh with you and show up when it counts. Gatherings are its natural setting, a birthday, a reunion, a toast to good news, any moment when joy is shared instead of kept private.

Community belongs here as well: a team, a group or a circle where you feel you belong and where good news is celebrated together. Small wins count; the card does not wait for something grand before it raises a glass.
Which people make you feel most like yourself, and when did you last celebrate something with them?

blocks.heading: What does the Three of Cups mean reversed?
paragraphs: Upside down, the Three of Cups can show feeling left out, watching the dance from the edge, or uneven friendships, where one person always makes the plans. Gossip, and a third person stepping between two friends, also belong to this side.

Overindulgence is the other reversed meaning: too much partying, too much of a good thing, social energy spent until little is left for you. Waite's reversed list has a line for this too, "the side of excess in physical enjoyment" (p. 220). A quiet evening with one friend who feels easy to be around can restore the balance.

blocks.heading: What does the Three of Cups mean in love?
paragraphs: Love under the Three of Cups is light and sociable: a romance that grows out of friendship, meeting someone through your circle, a relationship where you also have fun together. Joy is the point here, not drama.
With a partner, it favors shared celebrations and time with friends as a couple, while reminding you to keep your own friendships alive too.
A crowded heart is the reversed shade: a third person complicating things, gossip around a couple, or friends and partner pulling in different directions.

blocks.heading: What does the Three of Cups mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Teamwork that feels good is the career side: colleagues who cheer each other on, a project finished together, a network that opens doors. It is a strong card for collaboration, events and anything that depends on people.
Money under this card means plenty shared: spending on gatherings, gifts between friends, a sense of having enough to be generous. Reversed, it can describe overspending on nights out.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Three of Cups?
paragraphs: Send a friend a message today and suggest a simple plan: coffee, a walk, a call. Then keep it, and when you meet, toast to something small that went well.

blocks.heading: Is the Three of Cups a yes or no card?
The Three of Cups as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Among people, the Three of Cups is a good friend, the host who brings people together, or someone whose company makes everything lighter; you may recognize your own most sociable side in it. As feelings, the card speaks of fondness, fun and ease: enjoying someone's company, a warmth that may be friendly or the start of something more. Reversed, it describes mixed feelings in a group: someone left on the outside, or affection spread thin across too many people.

blocks.heading: The Three of Cups with other cards

pairs.text: Friends stand close at a hard moment, and shared sorrow weighs less.
Joy with nothing to hide: a bright, open celebration.
A team that works well and enjoys it. Mark the finished job together.
Between the party and time alone. Both have their place; notice which one you need.

blocks.heading: Three of Cups or Four of Wands?
paragraphs: Waite describes the Four of Wands as four staves holding up a great garland, with two women raising bunches of flowers beside a bridge that leads to an old manor house (p. 190); its meanings begin with country life, a haven of refuge, repose and harmony (p. 190). Modern readings call it celebration, homecoming and a stable base.
The Three of Cups celebrates people; the Four of Wands celebrates a place and a milestone.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Three of Cups
paragraphs: Who in my life makes me feel most like myself?
What small thing could I celebrate with someone soon?
Do my friendships feel balanced, or do I carry most of them?

faq.q: Is the Three of Cups a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good: few minor cards are this cheerful, all friendship, community and shared delight. Reversed, it asks you to look at which friendships give back and where a good time has turned into too much, which is worth noticing rather than a bad sign.

faq.q: Does the Three of Cups mean a love triangle?
faq.a: Only sometimes, and only reversed. Upright, the three figures are friends celebrating together. In a love question the reversed card can describe a third person or outside opinions crowding a relationship, but it remains a picture of the situation, not proof of anything.

faq.q: What does the Three of Cups mean for friendship?
faq.a: It is the friendship card of the whole deck. It describes friends who celebrate your wins, a group where you belong, or a reunion with people you have missed. Waite's maidens pledging one another (p. 220) are a toast between equals, and that is the spirit of it.

waite.quote: The conclusion of any matter in plenty, perfection and merriment; happy issue, victory, fulfilment, solace … Reversed: Expedition, dispatch, achievement, end.
